net.lemnik.eodsql

Interface BaseQuery

  • All Known Subinterfaces:
    TransactionQuery

    public interface BaseQuery

    The BaseQuery is the super-interface for any interface wishing to declare database queries. This validation is made by the QueryTool class when the implementation of a query is requested.

    Methods within a query implementation (subclass of BaseQuery) may declare throws SQLException, in which case database errors resulting from calls to that method will be thrown as normal checked exceptions. If the method does not declare the exception, it will be wrapped in a RuntimeException and thrown as an unchecked exception.

    Pooling vs. Non-Pooling

    Depending on how a BaseQuery is fetched from the QueryTool determines how Connections will be handled by the implementation. A BaseQuery fetched with a DataSource will not hold a Connection, but will instead hold onto the DataSource object (note that a BaseQuery implementation returned from QueryTool.getQuery(java.lang.Class) will hold a DataSource and not a Connection). When a query method is invoked, the implementation will fetch a Connection which will be used to perform the query.

    A "pooling" BaseQuery implementation (one wrapping a DataSource instead of a Connection) is safe to declare as a static variable. Pooling query implementations are the recommended way to work, unless you have good reason not to use them (ie: your database doesn't support pooling).

    public interface UserQuery extends BaseQuery {
        public static final UserQuery INSTANCE = QueryTool.getQuery(UserQuery.class);

        @Select("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?1")
        public User selectUserById(long id);
    }

    Non-Pooling BaseQuery objects wrap a single Connection object. This mechanism allows you to work with the Connection outside of the BaseQuery object, but is more expensive, since a BaseQuery instance must be constructed for each Connection object. To release the Connection you will need to invoke the close() method (which will invoke Connection.close().

    Since:
    1.0

    • Method Detail

      • close

        void close()

        Closes this BaseQuery, and releases any database resources it is currently holding. This method may throw an SQLException (wrapped in a RuntimeException if there is an underlying Connection object which throws an Exception from it's close() method.

        If this BaseQuery instance wraps a DataSource instead of a Connection object, this method will make the BaseQuery instance unusable. However, because pooling BaseQuery objects hold no real state resources they can be declared as static.

      • isClosed

        boolean isClosed()

        Determines whether this BaseQuery implementation has been closed. This method does not test to see whether the underlying Connection object (if there is one) has been closed. Thus the following code will return false:

        final Connection connection = DriverManager.getConnection(databaseURL);
        final UserQuery query = QueryTool.getQuery(connection);

        // do some work with the query here

        connection.close();

        return query.isClosed();

        Although the Connection object has been closed, the UserQuery object remains valid (since it has not yet been closed). Thus the exact contract of this method is that it will return true only when close() has been invoked on the same object.

        Returns:
        true if this BaseQuery has been closed
